newsitem.title: MOROCCO: King Hassan criticises former U.N. secretary-general.
newsitem.headline: King Hassan criticises former U.N. secretary-general.

text.p: Moroccan King Hassan criticised former U.N. secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali on his handling of the disputed Western Sahara, terming him "not a good mechanic" to get the issue resolved.
In an interview released on Wednesday, King Hassan said the Western Sahara issue was like an "engine out of order" with each side identifying the breakdown differently.

It was up to the U.N. secretary-general "to be the mechanic, to find the reasons for this blockage. For me, I think that the former secretary-general had not wanted, or had not been, a good mechanic for the Sahara affair.
"I hope that the new secretary-general (Kofi Annan) will be a better mechanic so that the engine is restored to running order," King Hassan said.

Under a U.N. peace plan, a referendum was to have been held in January 1992 to let the people of the former Spanish colony decide on integration with Morocco which claims the territory, or independence as sought by the Algerian-backed Polisario Front.

The ballot has has been stalled over who should be allowed to vote. Kofi Annan, who took over as U.N. secretary-general from Boutros-Ghali, this week appointed former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker as personal envoy for the Western Sahara.
